scientific_interpretation: Multiplying Source predicted deltas by a fixed small scalar, with measured truth/prior fixed and dependent features recomputed, is sufficient to reverse the observed in-sample U20 advantage over weighted distance in this artificial intervention.

This is not evidence that prediction scale uniquely or primarily caused the original Orion transfer failure. Source studies/predictors remain different; final risk models trained these Source records; no independent external or fresh-label replication was run.

The reversal combines a final-HGB U20 decline of0.079–0.105 with a larger distance U20 rise of0.157–0.174. Scaling also changes realized error ordering (rho0.746–0.960) and U20 oracle normalization; these changes are not separate causal percentages.

As s tends to0, squared prediction-prior discrepancy tends to prior mean-square magnitude, while squared realized error tends to truth mean-square magnitude. This algebra changes the risk problem and can favor distance; the experiment does not establish that this limiting explanation accounts quantitatively for its result.
Final ManualHGB still improves error@10 over distance in all four scaled macros. PrimaryU20 reversal does not establish uniform inferiority on all decision endpoints.

P-only brittleness and retained ManualHGB discrimination distinguish prediction-only extrapolation from collapse of the final Public-assisted model. This experiment does not isolate all Public components or establish transferable biological content.
Two Source architectures share the same575genes/1808tasks and one family; categorical agreement is not two independent laws or a publication-readiness result.
